subject.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]

question: Which pre-authentication resource boundary should SMS webhooks enforce while ensuring invalid traffic cannot consume valid-callback admission capacity for the same client key?
rationale: The proposed 300-request early gate only delays same-key quota poisoning, while moving all limiting after authentication changes the unauthenticated CPU boundary; choosing that permanent tradeoff requires owner intent.

options.title: Design a bypass-safe guard
options.body: Keep a bounded pre-authentication resource guard while ensuring authenticated callbacks do not share its consumable quota with rejected traffic.

options.title: Accept bounded same-key blocking
options.body: Keep the 300-request early gate and explicitly accept that a same-key invalid burst can temporarily reject valid callbacks.

options.title: Limit after validation
options.body: Rely on body-size or concurrency guards before applying separate invalid and valid quotas after authentication.

recommendation.title: Design a bypass-safe guard
recommendation.body: Keep a bounded pre-authentication resource guard while ensuring authenticated callbacks do not share its consumable quota with rejected traffic.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the latest security and availability hardening in this exact webhook path.
